findings.trigger: POST /tasks/add with {"container":"nginx","action":"stop","cycle":"daily","target_is_group":"false"} (a JSON string, not a boolean) -> bool("false") is True, the task is stored as targeting a GROUP named 'nginx' and answered 201 'created'. At run time the scheduler looks for a group, not the container, so the container the operator meant is never stopped, and nothing said so. This is exactly the shape update_task_status refused two functions further down (review D29, line 207) - the two routes in the same file now disagree about how a non-boolean is treated.
findings.suggestion: Treat target_is_group like is_active: accept only a real bool (or absence = False) and answer 400 otherwise; the same for status, which is taken from the request unchecked.
findings.unsure_why: TaskManagementService.add_task may verify that a group with that name exists and refuse; I cannot see it. The panel JS probably sends a real boolean, so a browser user may never hit this.

findings.trigger: POST /api/donation/submit with {"amount": 5, "publish_to_discord": "false"} -> the string is truthy, DonationRequest gets publish_to_discord=True and the donation is announced in every Discord channel although the caller switched publishing off. A message to Discord cannot be taken back. Same D29 class as F1; update_task_status was hardened for it, this route was not.
findings.suggestion: Accept only a real bool for publish_to_discord (absent = True), answer 400 for anything else - or let the service refuse it.
findings.unsure_why: The donation modal in the panel probably sends checkbox.checked (a real boolean); the service may also coerce. I cannot see either.

findings.trigger: POST /api/donation/submit without idempotency_key (an API caller, or a browser whose token generation failed - SPEC Z4 notes the randomUUID fallback exists because otherwise 'no token would be created at all') -> None is passed through; per SPEC Z4 the ledger then falls back to donor|amount|utcnow(), a clock-based key. A retry of the same request after the 30-second abort therefore books the amount a second time. Z4 says every donation carries a clock-independent key; the route is the boundary where a missing one could be refused and does not.
findings.suggestion: Refuse a missing or empty idempotency_key with 400 ('retry with the same token'), or have the service refuse it, so the guarantee does not depend on the client.
findings.unsure_why: The Z4 fix may have made the service refuse a missing key instead of falling back; SPEC only describes the fallback as the pre-fix state and the browser token as the fix. I cannot see progress_service / donation_service.

findings.trigger: First start with an action-log path that cannot be written (read-only mount, wrong owner) -> update_config_fields has already saved the password hash, then log_user_action raises OSError, the handler at line 988 answers {'success': false, 'error': 'Setup failed: Unable to save configuration'}. The operator believes no password exists; on the next attempt /setup answers 403 'closed'. The password they typed does work, but they were told the opposite. Second point at the same line: the call is positional - log_user_action("admin", "setup", "First-time ...") - while every other caller in this file uses action=/target=/source=/details= (line 365). If the parameters are in that order the action-log line reads action='admin', target='setup', source='First-time password setup completed', details empty.
findings.suggestion: Send the success answer before, or independently of, the audit line (log inside its own try and only log the failure); use keyword arguments like the other callers.
findings.unsure_why: log_user_action may swallow its own I/O errors, and I cannot see its signature - the positional order is inferred from line 365 only.

findings.trigger: Spam protection settings saved successfully, then log_user_action raises (unwritable action log -> OSError is not in either except tuple -> Flask 500 page; or settings['global_settings'] is not a dict -> AttributeError -> 500 'Service error: Unable to save spam protection settings'). The settings ARE saved, the operator is told they are not, and saves again or gives up. Z3 in reverse.
findings.suggestion: Log after or independently of the answer; build the details string from the validated config object rather than the raw request dict.
findings.unsure_why: problems_in() may already guarantee global_settings is a dict, and log_user_action may not raise; both are outside this section.

findings.trigger: POST /api/mech/difficulty with {"difficulty_multiplier": "nan", "manual_override": true} (or "inf", 0, -1) -> float() accepts all of these, no range check in the route; a NaN/zero/negative multiplier reaches the difficulty setting and every level cost derived from it becomes NaN, zero or negative - the mech either never levels or levels on the first cent, and the panel shows those numbers as fact. Also: {"difficulty_multiplier": null} -> float(None) is a TypeError, which no handler here lists -> raw 500 HTML to a JSON client; and manual_override is used by truthiness, so the string "false" selects the 'set' branch (D29 class again).
findings.suggestion: Reject non-finite and non-positive values (and an upper bound) in the route or make sure the service does; add TypeError to the 400 handler; treat manual_override as a strict bool.
findings.unsure_why: MechWebService.manage_difficulty may validate the range itself; the panel's input probably has min/max. I cannot see either.

findings.trigger: Two related shapes. (a) A plain form submit without the X-Requested-With header (JS disabled, or a fetch that omits the header) -> success and 'save_result.success == False' both end in a bare redirect to the config page: nothing is flashed on either path, so a rejected save comes back as the old values with no message. (b) On the three exception paths flash() is called AND JSON is returned; for an AJAX caller the flash is not consumed, so the banner 'Service error: Unable to save configuration.' appears on the next full page load - possibly after a later save that succeeded, telling the operator that one failed.
findings.suggestion: Flash the outcome on the non-AJAX path (both success and failure); on the AJAX path do not flash at all.
findings.unsure_why: Whether the panel ever submits this form without the header depends on the JS I cannot see.

findings.trigger: POST /set_ui_language with ui_language='' or 'xx' (or any string) -> written into the configuration unchecked and answered {'success': true}. Every later page render asks for a locale that does not exist; what the templates then show (English fallback, missing strings, or an error) depends on the locale loader.
findings.suggestion: Accept only codes for which a locale file exists (or a fixed allow-list) and answer 400 otherwise.
findings.unsure_why: update_config_fields or the locale loader may validate/fall back; the dropdown in the panel only offers valid codes, so a browser user would need a crafted request.

findings.trigger: GET /api/mech/status with total_donated = 12.99 or amount_needed = 0.5 in the service answer -> _safe_int does int(value), so 12.99 becomes 12 and 0.5 becomes 0, returned under success: true. If these values are dollars (not cents), the reported totals are wrong and look authoritative. Second point, line 1259: _safe_string discards any string containing 'line ' or 'Error:' - a level name like 'Online Titan' or 'Frontline Guard' is reported as 'Unknown'.
findings.suggestion: Keep floats as floats (round to 2 decimals) for monetary fields; drop the substring blacklist or restrict it to fields that could carry an exception text.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see the unit of total_donated/amount_needed in get_current_status(), the level names, or whether anything in the panel reads this endpoint.

findings.trigger: The limit is exactly 60.0 s and the comment says it matches the client's auto-refresh interval - zero tolerance. The first request pays connection setup (TCP/TLS) and arrives late relative to its send time; the next one, 60 s later on a kept-alive connection, arrives earlier -> elapsed 59.9 s -> 429 'TOO MANY REQUESTS' as the body of the log pane instead of the log. Same when two admins share one address (reverse proxy, NAT): the second one's every request within a minute of the first is refused. Also _last_log_request is never pruned.
findings.suggestion: Set the interval visibly below the client interval (e.g. 55 s) or key the limiter on the session rather than the address; prune old entries.
findings.unsure_why: The client's actual interval and how it renders a 429 are in JS I cannot see.

notes: F2 and F3 both belong to submit_donation (main_routes.py:471); the verdict names F3 as the more serious of the two. Things read and NOT counted as findings: (1) _get_cached_mech_state (line 27) is defined but never called in this file; its two compat classes are identical duplicates; the log line at :38 formats cache_age_seconds with :.1f, so a None there would be a TypeError caught at :82 and turn a cache HIT into 'None' without even trying the direct service - only if that field can be None, which I cannot tell. (2) add_task and edit_task_route call _player_warnings(result.task_data) twice each (:92-93, :339-340), i.e. query_problems() runs twice per successful request - waste, not a wrong result. (3) add_task takes status=data.get('status','pending') from the client unchecked; whether an arbitrary status is meaningful is up to the service. (4) show_task_form's fallback hard-codes timezone 'Europe/Berlin'/'CEST' when the service fails; with active_containers=[] the form should not be submittable, so the wrong zone likely cannot reach a task. (5) retime_tasks_route: if retime_tasks raises midway, some tasks are moved and the answer is 500 'Data error moving tasks' with no count - whether it is all-or-nothing is in code I cannot see. (6) get_donation_status, mech_animation, the mech music and mech display routes carry no login; the comment at :422-425 shows public READ routes are known and only the write route was closed, so treated as intended. (7) game_query_retest: if set_testing(True) at :563 raises a ValueError (e.g. a corrupt verdicts JSON -> JSONDecodeError) the operator is told 'Invalid request' 400 - misleading text, but loud. Any logged-in caller can also write arbitrary container names into the verdicts file. (8) mech_animation/port_diagnostics/get_mech_music_*: on failure they pass result.status_code through; if a service ever leaves it None Flask answers 200 with an error body - depends on the services. (9) delete_donation and set/reset_mech_difficulty write no log_user_action line, unlike spam protection and setup; the ledger itself records the compensation event, so the deletion is not silent. (10) save_config_api logs every display_name value at INFO ([DISPLAY_NAME_SAVE_DEBUG]) - noise. (11) performance_stats has no handler for ValueError/TypeError/KeyError -> raw 500 HTML; loud, not wrong. (12) get_mech_display_image sends a constant ETag with a 24 h public cache; Flask does not evaluate If-None-Match here, so it is only advisory. (13) discord_bot_setup hands the whole config dict to its template; whether the template renders the (encrypted) token is outside this section. (14) setup_save: two concurrent first-time POSTs before a hash exists both pass setup_is_closed; last write wins - edge case at first start only. (15) SPEC B14 appears twice with two different contents (scheduler skip on unreadable config, and the $10,000 donation cap) - a numbering slip in the spec, not in the code.
